technocore.head_message:
perf(stats): maintained room totals, and serve /stats stale while it refreshes (#858)

## What

`/stats` stops asking the filesystem for two numbers the store already
maintains, and stops making the caller wait for the walk it still has.
An expired entry is served as it stands while one refresh runs behind
it; a window of `0` still means no cache at all.

## Why

Verified on `20a4457`, against the live deployment (239k rooms, 3.5M
notes):

| | |
|---|---|
| `/stats` with a correct token | **no answer within 120 s** |
| `service_stats` walk, warm | 3.26 s — **2.32 s of it `stat()`** (71%)
|
| same walk without the `stat()` | 0.94 s |
| `room_stats(limit=50)` walk, warm (called for the engagement rollup) |
3.70 s |

`USAGE_FILE` already holds the room count and bytes, maintained by the
create path and the reaper — the same integers `MAX_ROOMS` is enforced
against, so taking the count from there also stops the gauge and the
refusal disagreeing. The byte half is only settled by a reap, so it is
measured when no reap has run yet.

Blocking on the refresh was the other half: the walk outgrew the 45 s
timeout of the 4-hourly digest this endpoint exists for, and because
each poll started another walk, misses arrived faster than they cleared.

This is the `/stats` half only. `room_stats` still stats every room for
the recency sort —
[#576](https://github.com/flop-labs/technocore-chat/issues/576) proposes
the recency index that would retire both walks, and I have left it alone
rather than compete with it.

One judgement call for you: `core/app.py` grows 5 code-lines (1020 →
1025, cap 1030). `sz.py --caps` passes; the ratchet in
`sz-baseline.json` is yours to regenerate, so I have not touched it.

## Checks

- [x] `coverage run -m pytest tests -q` — 773 passed, 1 skipped
- [x] `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .` — clean; `ty check` — one
pre-existing warning in `tests/unit/test_counter_batching.py`, unchanged
on `main`
- [x] Docs: none describe this; the two docstrings carry the reasoning
- [x] New surface on a world-writable service: **nothing new** — same
token gate, same payload; an unauthenticated caller still gets the
byte-identical 404
